papers.title: Topological passivation makes high strength alloys insensitive to hydrogen embrittlement
papers.abstract: Infrastructure parts for a hydrogen (H) economy need alloys that are mechanically strong and at the same time resistant to the most dangerous and abrupt type of failure mode, namely, H embrittlement. These two properties are in fundamental conflict, as increasing strength typically amplifies susceptibility to H-related failure. Here, we introduce a new approach to make alloys resistant to H embrittlement, by creating a topological passivation layer (up to a few hundred micrometers thick) near the material surface, the region that is most vulnerable to H ingress and attack. It features instead a layer of ultrafine laminated grains with tens of times higher dislocation density than conventional materials, altering H diffusion, trapping and crack evolution. We tested the concept on a face-centered cubic (FCC) CoCrNi medium entropy model alloy which undergoes severe H-induced intergranular cracking. Two key mechanisms create the topological passivation: First, the high density (up to ~1.3e15 m-2) of H-trapping dislocations within the passivating grain layer decelerates H migration by up to about an order of magnitude, delaying H-induced crack initiation at grain boundaries. More importantly, once unavoidable micro-sized H-induced intergranular cracks emerge in the topmost surface region, they become completely arrested by the laminated grains, due to a transition in the embrittlement mechanism from H-enhanced grain boundary decohesion to highly energy-dissipative dislocation-associated cracking. These effects almost completely eliminate H embrittlement, at even doubled yield strength, when exposing the so architected material to harsh H attack. Our approach leverages surface mechanical treatments to tailor metallic microstructures in surface regions most susceptible to H attack, providing a scalable solution to protect alloys from H-induced damage.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究高强度合金的氢脆问题，虽涉及力学性能但与增材制造直接无关。
llm.why_not_core: The paper does not involve additive manufacturing fabrication; the material processing is surface mechanical treatment, not AM.

summary_zh.motivation: 解决高强度合金强度与氢脆敏感性之间的矛盾。
summary_zh.method: 在材料表面构建拓扑钝化层，包含超细层状晶粒和高密度位错。
summary_zh.result: 在屈服强度加倍条件下几乎完全消除氢脆。
summary_zh.validation: 通过力学测试和微观表征验证氢脆抑制效果。

summary_en.motivation: To resolve the fundamental conflict between mechanical strength and hydrogen embrittlement susceptibility in high-strength alloys.
summary_en.method: A topological passivation layer with ultrafine laminated grains and high dislocation density is created via surface mechanical treatment.
summary_en.result: Hydrogen embrittlement is almost completely eliminated even at doubled yield strength under severe hydrogen attack.
summary_en.validation: The concept is validated by mechanical testing and microstructural characterization after hydrogen exposure.
